t.7.54.1: When this had been said, Rāma, with joined palms, replied to those sages: "What does Lavaṇa eat, what is his conduct, and where does he dwell?"
t.7.54.2: Having heard the words of Rāghava, all those sages then related to him how Lavaṇa had grown in power.
t.7.54.3: His food is all living creatures, and ascetics above all; his conduct is ever ferocity, and his dwelling is always in Madhuvana.
t.7.54.4: Having slain ten thousand lions, tigers, deer and elephants, and men as well, he constantly makes of them his daily meal.
t.7.54.6: Having heard those words, Rāghava said to the great sages: "I shall have that Rākṣasa slain; let your fear depart."
t.7.54.5: Then that mighty one, devouring other creatures, was like Antaka with his mouth gaping wide when the time of universal destruction has come.
t.7.54.7: Having thus given his promise to those sages of fierce splendor, Raghunandana spoke to all his brothers gathered together.
t.7.54.8: Who will slay Lavaṇa, O heroes? Whose share shall that task be made: that of mighty-armed Bharata, or else of Śatrughna?
t.7.54.9: Thus addressed by Rāghava, Bharata spoke these words: "I will slay him; let that be assigned as my share."
t.7.54.10: Having heard Bharata's words, full of heroism and valour, the younger brother of Lakṣmaṇa left his golden seat and stood up.
t.7.54.11: Then Śatrughna, bowing low before the lord of men, spoke these words: 'The mighty-armed middle scion of Raghu has already accomplished his task.'
t.7.54.12: For long ago the deserted city of Ayodhyā was guarded by the noble one, who kept anguish in his heart as he awaited the noble one's return.
t.7.54.13: And many sorrows have been endured here, O king, by the great-souled one, as he lay upon beds of hardship in Nandigrāma.
t.7.54.14: Having lived on fruits and roots and worn matted locks and bark garments, this delight of the Rāghavas has endured such sorrow; while I stand here as your servant, O king, he should not suffer hardship again.
t.7.54.15: When Śatrughna spoke thus, Rāghava spoke again: "Let it be so, Kākutstha; let my command be carried out."
t.7.54.16: I shall consecrate you to the kingship in the fair city of Madhu. O mighty-armed one, if you have regard for Bharata, let Bharata remain settled here.
t.7.54.17: You are brave and accomplished in learning, and capable of settling the city once occupied by Madhu, as well as the fair countryside around it.
t.7.54.18: For he who, having uprooted the lineage of a king, does not then install a king there upon its destruction, goes to hell.
t.7.54.19: So you, having slain Lavaṇa, the son of Madhu, whose resolve is fixed on evil, rule the kingdom righteously, if you have regard for my word.
t.7.54.20: O hero, no reply is to be made while I am speaking; the command of an elder brother must be carried out by the younger, of this there is no doubt.
t.7.54.21: And accept, O Kākutstha, the consecration I have prepared, conducted by the brahmins headed by Vasiṣṭha with the prescribed rites and mantras.
